summary: Depth-first rabbithole dossier for Salvage Auction Bidding Strategy; source-anchored research pack.

facts.text: This report covers the internal mechanism of bidding strategy at online salvage vehicle auctions: the auction rules a bidder is playing against, the parts a strategy is built from, the invariants the strategy must respect, and the points where the strategy stops working.

**C2. Proxy bidding that carries the preliminary high bidder into the live stage is part of the patented claim set, not a convenience feature.** Claim 2 provides that "if said specific period of time expires before a current preliminary bid on said item reaches said proxy bid, entering a new bid during said sale of said item." Claims 3–5 cover countdown mechanics that inform bidders of impending closure and reset on a new bid. <https://patents.google.com/patent/US7315832B2/en>

**U2. Whether the winner's curse actually binds for professional, repeat salvage bidders.** The experimental literature says it persists even among experienced subjects (https://www.asc.ohio-state.edu/kagel.4/CVsurvey.short.PDF). The field literature contains a long-standing counter-position: Capen, Clapp and Campbell (1971) read offshore oil lease returns as evidence of overbidding, while Hendricks and Porter (1988) concluded the bid patterns were consistent with rational behaviour by experienced bidders (see Hendricks, Porter and Tan, https://www.nber.org/papers/w9836 and https://onlinelibra

**C8. The buyer's cost is not the hammer price: buyer transaction fees are tiered by price and sit alongside several fixed per-transaction charges.** RB Global FY2024 10-K: transactional buyer revenue "includes buyer transaction fees based on a tiered structure earned from purchasers upon purchase of an asset, as well as other auction-related fees earned from buyers to complete the purchase of an asset, such as title processing, late pick-up, salvage buyer platform registration and other administrative processing charges." Copart's 10-K similarly lists "vehicle purchasing fees" among its aucti

**C9. In several states, bidding at a salvage pool is restricted by statute to licensed dismantlers or their agents, which forces retail buyers through a broker and inserts a principal-agent layer into the bid.** Alabama Administrative Code r. 810-5-12-.06 states that "Section 40-12-421, Code of Ala. 1975, restricts sales at salvage pools or salvage disposal sales to persons holding a current automotive dismantler and parts recycler license or their agents or employees," and that the Buyer's Identification (BID) card "shall be available to any person, firm, or corporation that possesses a curr

This report covers how a buyer decides what to bid on a damaged or total-loss vehicle at a salvage auction, and what determines whether that bid was correct after the fact. It covers the auction mechanism the bid is submitted into, the cost components that sit between the hammer price and the landed cost, the reliability of the valuation inputs the platform supplies, the experimental evidence on how bidders in this class of auction actually behave, and the market conditions as of Q1 2026.

**B4. The landed cost, not the hammer price, is what the maximum must be set against.** Copart's fees are contractual add-ons on top of the bid: "vehicle purchasing fees, vehicle listing fees, and vehicle selling fees that can be based on a predetermined percentage of the vehicle sales price, tiered vehicle sales price driven fees, or at a fixed fee based on the sale of each vehicle regardless of the selling price of the vehicle." (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/900075/000090007523000034/cprt-20230731.htm) Because part of the fee load is a percentage of the bid, the fee is not a const

**D1. Fee scaling breaks linear max-bid rules.** Because a percentage-of-price component sits on top of the bid (B4), a rule of the form "bid up to X% of after-repair value" overstates the true ceiling by the marginal fee rate at the bid level reached. The rule must be applied to landed cost, solved backwards from the exit price.

**G1. The marginal bidder is frequently not a rebuilder, so rebuild economics do not set the clearing price.** Copart's FY2017 Form 10-K states that "Vehicle dismantlers" are "the largest group of vehicle buyers, based on volume of vehicles purchased," and that "For fiscal 2017, sales of U.S. vehicles, on a unit basis, to members registered outside the state where the vehicle was located accounted for 49.8% of total vehicles sold; 29.7% of vehicles were sold to out of state members within the U.S. and 20.1% were sold to International members." `[read]` — https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data

**A1. The salvage auction is a two-stage mechanism: an extended preliminary bidding period followed by a short internet-only live auction.** Copart's own SEC filing states: "The VB3 technology and model employs a two-step bidding process. The first step is an open preliminary bidding feature that allows members to enter bids over the internet during the preview period... Preliminary bidding ends at a specified time prior to the start of a second bidding step, an internet-only virtual auction." (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/900075/000090007523000034/cprt-20230731.htm)

**A6. The live stage uses a soft close, not a hard close.** A countdown timer runs, and when a new bid arrives "the countdown ceases and resets a preestablished number of seconds later"; the reset interval may shrink as bidding continues (the patent gives thirty seconds falling to fifteen after three minutes). (https://patents.google.com/patent/US7315832B2/en)

**B1. The auction is a two-stage ascending mechanism, not a single sealed bid, so a bidding strategy has to specify behaviour in both stages.** Copart's FY2025 Form 10-K describes VB3: members first submit maximum bids during a preview period, during which the BID4U feature bids incrementally on their behalf up to that maximum; a live virtual auction then lets bidders bid against each other and against the high preliminary bidder while BID4U continues to submit bids for that bidder. https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/900075/000162828025042946/cprt-20250731.htm

**B3. The value estimate itself is unusually noisy because the platform disclaims the condition data it publishes.** Copart's member terms state vehicles are sold "AS-IS WHERE-IS," without warranty, that Copart and its sellers "expressly disclaim the accuracy or completeness of any and all information provided," and that "It is the sole responsibility of Member to ascertain, confirm, research, inspect and/or investigate vehicles and any and all Vehicle Information prior to bidding on vehicles." (https://www.copart.com/Content/us/en/Member-Terms-and-Conditions) *Retrieval note: copart.com serve

**D5. The winner's-curse framing is contested as an explanation of field outcomes.** Kagel and Levin themselves record that the claim "was greeted with skepticism by many economists as it implies that bidders repeatedly err," note that cartel/coordination theory offers "an alternative and simpler explanation," and state plainly that "It is exceedingly difficult to support claims of a winner's curse using field data because of reliability problems with the data and because alternative explanations for overbidding are often available." (https://www.asc.ohio-state.edu/kagel.4/CVsurvey.short.PDF)

**G2. A strategy must be judged on the full bid population, not on wins alone, because conditioning on wins is precisely the selection effect that produces the curse.** Kagel and Levin's measure of the curse is the difference between a bidder's unconditional estimate and the expected value conditional on holding the highest signal. https://www.asc.ohio-state.edu/kagel.4/CVsurvey.short.PDF

This report covers how a bidder sets and places bids for insurance total-loss and other salvage vehicles at the North American salvage pools — chiefly Copart and IAA. It traces the mechanism the bidder faces (how the auction actually closes, what a proxy bid does, who is allowed to bid, what the winning bid costs in total) and the value inputs that determine whether a winning bid was correct.

**C4. The mechanism is materially unchanged twenty-two years later, now branded VB3.** Copart's FY2025 Form 10-K (period ended 2025-07-31, filed 2025-09-26) states: "Members enter the maximum price they are willing to pay for a vehicle and VB3's BID4U feature incrementally bids on the vehicle on their behalf during all phases of the auction," and "When bidding stops, a countdown is initiated. If no bids are received during the countdown, the vehicle sells to the highest bidder." <https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/900075/000162828025042946/cprt-20250731.htm>

It uses the two US salvage platforms that set the rules for the category — Copart and IAA (Insurance Auto Auctions) — as the concrete instance of those rules, because their platform mechanics are documented in primary sources (a granted patent, SEC filings, a published policy).

**D2. The proxy mechanism only approximates a second price.** With enforced minimum increments (A5) and seller approval on a share of lots (C1), the price paid is not the second-highest valuation; bidding one's true reservation price is close to optimal but not exactly a dominant strategy in the textbook sense.

**E6. The ascending (English) format mitigates the curse but does not remove it, which matters because salvage auctions use exactly this format.** Kagel and Levin state the winner's curse is alive and well for inexperienced bidders in both English and first-price auctions, although clearly less severe in English auctions; for more experienced bidders the comparative-static predictions of the Nash model are largely satisfied in English auctions, with bidders following a simple rule of thumb that yields nearly the same prices as the Nash model. https://www.asc.ohio-state.edu/kagel.4/CVsurvey.sho

**C2. Copart sells a paid escape from C1, which converts the stated maximum into a soft maximum.** "Increment bidding" authorises Copart "to increase an entered maximum bid by one and only one increment in the event a Virtual Bidder ties your entered maximum bid." Copart's own worked example: a $5,000 increment-enabled preliminary bid against a $5,000 virtual bid results in the lot selling to the preliminary bidder at $5,100. `[read]` — https://www.copart.com/content/us/en/pdfs/terms&conditions-2019.pdf *Boundary condition:* the disciplined "hard maximum" that most bidding advice prescribes is

**A4. Title brands follow the vehicle across state lines, so brand-washing by retitling in another state is not a reliable value-recovery strategy.** NMVTIS maintains title, odometer and brand information such as "flood" or "rebuilt" even when a vehicle changes title from one state to another. https://vehiclehistory.bja.ojp.gov/nmvtis_understandingvhr

**B2. The sale closes on a countdown, which is what makes last-second bidding possible and makes a walk-away number necessary in advance.** Copart states that when bidding stops a countdown is initiated, and if no bids are received during the countdown the vehicle sells to the highest bidder. https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/900075/000162828025042946/cprt-20250731.htm

**B3. Once accepted, an online bid is effectively irrevocable, so there is no strategy that relies on retracting a bid.** The registration terms for a Copart broker state that once the system accepts an online bid it can only be deleted for sealed bid sales, and instruct buyers to be careful when placing bids. https://www.copart.com/content/us/en/pdfs/terms%20&%20conditions_01082020.pdf

**G3. A useful diagnostic for the winner's curse is the share of won lots whose realised margin is negative, benchmarked against the experimental finding that overbidding shows up as a majority of high bids exceeding the conditional value.** In the inexperienced-bidder data, 82% of high bids exceeded that value and only 17% of auctions produced positive profits. https://www.asc.ohio-state.edu/kagel.4/CVsurvey.short.PDF

Hendricks, K., Porter, R. H. & Tan, G., *Bidding Rings and the Winner's Curse: The Case of

**C12. Whether a given damaged car reaches a salvage auction with a branded title at all is a state-law variable, not a property of the damage, so the same physical car has a different exit value depending on jurisdiction.** State total-loss thresholds are expressed either as a percentage of pre-loss value or as a "total loss formula"; published compilations put the percentage range roughly between 50% and 100%. This claim rests on a secondary compilation (a law-firm 50-state chart), not a federal register — see Disagreements. <https://www.mwl-law.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/02/AUTOMOBILE-TOTA

**C17. The popular "snipe in the last seconds" tactic, imported from eBay, has no theoretical basis at Copart and is mechanically defeated by proxy bidding.** Roth and Ockenfels show that late bidding is an equilibrium phenomenon specifically under a *fixed* end time, because "very late bids have a positive probability of not being successfully submitted, and this opens a way for bidders to implicitly collude, and avoid bidding wars, in auctions such as those run by eBay, which have a fixed end time." They find "significantly more late bidding on eBay than on Amazon," where the auction is exte

**B7. Supply into the channel is at a record high and skewed old.** CCC's Crash Course reporting puts total-loss frequency at a record 23.1% of auto claims in 2025, with more than 70% of total-loss valuations on vehicles seven years or older. (https://www.cccis.com/news-and-insights/posts/ccc-crash-course-2026-report-finds-higher-severity-and-record-total-loss-frequency) The inventory a strategy is bidding on is therefore dominated by low-ACV, older units.

**B6. In at least one studied online ascending automobile auction, a small group of buyers behaved like sellers' agents, meaning the standing price a bidder reacts to may not reflect genuine rival demand. [adjacent-platform]** Grether, Porter and Shum ran a field experiment with an online used-automobile ascending auction company across two sites, manipulating the price grid. In the Texas auctions they found bidding patterns among a small but prominent group of buyers suggesting they were cyber-shills working on behalf of sellers; these patterns did not appear in the New York auctions. https:/

**F1. Supply into salvage auctions is at a record high, which is the pro-buyer side of the current market.** CCC's Crash Course 2026 report, released 2026-03-31, reports total loss frequency reached 23.1% of claims, a new industry high. https://finance.yahoo.com/sectors/healthcare/articles/ccc-crash-course-2026-report-120000680.html

1. **Whether salvage auction margins are structurally positive at all.** Vendor guidance implies a reliable 40–60% recovery band (https://blog.autobidmaster.com/2026/02/a-rule-of-thumb-for-buying-salvage-vehicles-at-auction/), while Copart's own filing states its platform exists to increase what buyers are willing to pay (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/900075/000162828025042946/cprt-20250731.htm). No independent measurement of realised buyer-side returns was found. This is the central unresolved question and the deliberate disconfirming search did not resolve it in the heuristic's fav

**B6. The exit-value anchor drifts with the wholesale market, so a fixed percentage rule silently re-prices itself.** The Manheim Used Vehicle Value Index read 212.3 in February 2026, up 4% year over year, and 215.3 in March 2026, up 6.2% year over year. (https://www.coxautoinc.com/insights/manheim-used-vehicle-value-index-february-2026-trends/; https://www.coxautoinc.com/insights/manheim-used-vehicle-value-index-march-2026-trends/) A maximum bid expressed as a share of after-repair value inherits this drift.

**E5. Maximum recoverable liability decays 10% per month and terminates at 90 days.** IAA: "The Company's liability, if any, shall be limited to the sale price of the Vehicle, less 10% per month from the sale date. All liability of the Company, if any, shall terminate 90 days after the sale date." `[read]` — https://ca.iaai.com/Content/Documents/IAAPoliciesJuly2020_en.pdf *Boundary condition:* the recoverable ceiling is the sale price only — never the repair spend, transport, storage, or lost margin. Any strategy whose downside case assumes recovery of sunk repair cost is miscalibrated.

**F5. The upstream supply of salvage lots is itself set by state-varying total loss thresholds, so lot quality is not comparable across states.** Total loss thresholds range from roughly 60% to 100% of pre-accident value depending on state, with some states instead applying a total loss formula (repair cost + salvage value ≥ ACV). `[snippet]` — https://www.mwl-law.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/02/AUTOMOBILE-TOTAL-LOSS-THRESHOLDS-CHART.pdf `[snippet]` — https://www.carinsurance.com/Articles/total-loss-thresholds.aspx *Boundary condition:* a lot titled salvage in a 60%-threshold state is, on avera

**U3. Whether IAA's 70%-of-sole-pre-bid rule (C3) applies in the United States.** Confirmed in IAA's Canadian Auction Policies (July 2020). IAA's US auction rules page returns a bot-detection interstitial to automated retrieval, so I could not verify or refute a US equivalent. A bidder should verify this against their own jurisdiction's rules before relying on it.

**C14. The bidder pool is national and international, which removes local-scarcity arguments from the strategy.** Copart FY2025 10-K: a database of "approximately 1 million registered members ('buyers')"; for fiscal 2025, 69.8% of US vehicles sold went to members registered outside the state where the vehicle was located (31.0% out-of-state domestic, 38.8% international). The FY2024 10-K gives the comparable figure as 68.4%. <https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/900075/000162828025042946/cprt-20250731.htm> <https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/900075/000090007524000024/cprt-20240731.htm>

**D5. The common practitioner heuristic — a repaired salvage vehicle retains 40–60% of clean-title value — originates in vendor marketing content and is not supported here by any primary measurement.** It is reported as a starting point to be adjusted for repair cost and condition. https://blog.autobidmaster.com/2026/02/a-rule-of-thumb-for-buying-salvage-vehicles-at-auction/

**E2. The required downward adjustment is large and grows with the number of rivals, which is the opposite of the intuition that a busy lot justifies bidding harder.** In the Kagel–Levin design, the bid reduction needed *just* to avoid losing money on average is 60% of the signal-noise parameter with 4 bidders and 75% of it with 7 bidders. https://www.asc.ohio-state.edu/kagel.4/CVsurvey.short.PDF

**F3. The composition of salvage inventory is shifting toward older vehicles, which shortens the resale runway on a rebuild.** 72% of total loss valuations involve vehicles seven years or older, and 46% of repairable vehicles are seven years or older. https://www.autobodynews.com/news/calibrations-surge-past-35-of-repairs-as-total-losses-head-toward-second-straight-record
**H7. Assume the price is set by non-local demand. With 38.8% of US units going to international members, a local repair-cost advantage does not translate into a bidding advantage.** B5.

2. **Magnitude of the branded-title discount.** The *Cohen* pleading put the ERV-to-salvage gap at 20–40% (https://blog.ericgoldman.org/archives/2022/10/section-230-applies-to-sellers-listings-on-auto-auction-service-cohen-v-copart.htm); TxDMV says only "substantially less" (https://www.txdmv.gov/motorists/buying-or-selling-a-vehicle/title-check-look-before-you-buy/rebuilt). These are not the same quantity — one is a pre-repair salvage discount, the other a post-rebuild resale discount — and no source reconciles them.

This report covers only the act of **deciding what to bid, and how to bid it, at an insurance salvage auction** (Copart, IAA/Insurance Auto Auctions and their affiliates). It targets the boundary conditions under which a bidding strategy stops working, the mechanical failure modes of the bidding platforms themselves, and evidence that disconfirms the popular "max bid = retail value − repair cost − margin" formula.

**A7. The soft close is what makes last-second sniping unprofitable here.** Roth and Ockenfels (AER 2002) compared eBay's fixed end time ("hard close") with Amazon's rule of automatic extension "past the scheduled end time until ten minutes have passed without a bid" (soft close), and found "the fraction of bids submitted in the closing seconds of the auction is substantially larger in eBay than in Amazon, and more experience causes bidders to bid later on eBay, but earlier on Amazon." (https://web.stanford.edu/class/cs206/roth-ockenfels.pdf) Because a salvage lot's timer resets on every bid (

**C2. Salvage lots are outside the platform's arbitration protection.** Copart's Wholesale Auction Arbitration Policy (effective October 17, 2025) states that "Green and Yellow Light ratings apply to vehicles that are both whole-car, clean title vehicles in the Wholesale Auction AND are eligible for arbitration as outlined in this Policy," and that the policy "only applies to qualifying Green Light and Yellow Light vehicle purchases and transactions." (https://www.copart.com/content/us/en/landing-page/wholesale/arbitrationpolicy-en-oct-2025.pdf) This is the hardest invariant in the concept: on

**B1. A salvage lot is a common-value object, so the bid must be shaded below the bidder's own estimate.** Kagel and Levin define the common-value case as one where "the value of the item is the same to everyone but different bidders have different estimates about the underlying value," and describe the failure mode precisely: bidders who bid their own unconditional estimate ignore "the fact that you only win when your estimate happens to be the highest," so "winning against a number of rivals following similar bidding strategies implies that your estimate is an overestimate of the value... Un

**B2. On seller-approval lots the bidder holds a binding offer while the seller holds a free option.** Under IAA's "If Bid" mechanism, when bids do not reach the reserve the seller has 24 hours (or another announced window) to accept, and "The bidder may not withdraw the If Bid during the If Bid time frame." `[read]` — https://ca.iaai.com/Content/Documents/IAAPoliciesJuly2020_en.pdf *Failure mode:* this is an asymmetric option written by the bidder for free. A strategy that models bid value without pricing the option premium is systematically overbidding on reserve lots. The seller exercises o

**D4. Condition uncertainty cannot be resolved by more pre-bid research past a point,** because the platform disclaims the data it supplies (B3) and provides no recourse on salvage (C2). Beyond in-person inspection, the residual variance is irreducible and belongs in the shading term (B1), not in a better estimate.

**C5. Walking away from a win is expensive and escalates to loss of access.** Copart's terms set a relist fee of "$400 USD or 10% of the sale price (whichever is greater)" plus the $200 transaction fee and forfeiture of the security deposit, with excessive relisting triggering suspension. Payment is due by 5:00 pm on the third business day; a $50 late fee applies, and non-payment within seven business days forfeits the full security deposit. `[read]` — https://www.copart.com/content/us/en/pdfs/terms&conditions-2019.pdf IAA: unpaid vehicles "may be re-sold at the next auction sale on an unreser

**C6. Bidding capacity is collateral-constrained, not judgement-constrained.** Copart's broker terms require a $400 minimum security deposit supporting up to $4,000 of bid allowance on one vehicle at a time, with $100 per additional $1,000 of allowance and a further $400 deposit per simultaneous vehicle count. `[read]` — https://www.copart.com/content/us/en/pdfs/terms&conditions-2019.pdf *Failure mode:* a portfolio strategy that plans to bid on N lots to win one requires N× the deposit. Bidders who do not post it discover the constraint mid-sale, which forces bidding on the wrong lot of the da

**D3. The platform states outright that hidden damage is normal and extensive repair is the expectation.** IAA: "Most Vehicles have significant damage, defects, flaws and/or wear and tear. Not all damage is visible and some damage may be hidden." Its arbitration section repeats: "Most Vehicles sold at auction have hidden damage and generally require extensive repair or are not capable of repair and Buyers should allow for this when bidding." `[read]` — https://ca.iaai.com/Content/Documents/IAAPoliciesJuly2020_en.pdf *Failure mode:* photograph-based repair estimation has a structurally one-side

**E6. Risk of loss transfers at bid acceptance, before payment and before pickup.** Copart: "Buyer takes full responsibility and assumes all risk of loss for all vehicles purchased from the time auction accepts Buyer's bid," and disclaims responsibility for "theft or vandalism, or acts of God" while the vehicle sits on its lot. `[read]` — https://www.copart.com/content/us/en/pdfs/terms&conditions-2019.pdf IAA: "The Company does not provide insurance coverage for Vehicles... Risk of loss on a purchased vehicle passes to Buyer once the vehicle has been awarded to Buyer." `[read]` — https://ca.ia

**G3. Exchange rates move the level of competition, so a strategy calibrated in one FX regime decalibrates in another.** Copart's filings note that the dollar exchange rate to foreign currencies "has an impact on auction participation by international buyers." `[snippet, from 10-K search extract]` — https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000900075/000090007517000044/cprt07312017-10k.htm *Failure mode:* a bidder who back-tests a max-bid rule on a period of dollar strength will find it loses far more auctions during dollar weakness, with no change in the vehicles themselves.

**G4. The winner's curse is the structurally correct prior for this market, and it persists with experience.** Kagel and Levin's survey of common-value auction experiments concludes that inexperienced bidders are strongly susceptible to the winner's curse, that losses decline with experience, but that the effect persists; it arises from failure to condition on the adverse-selection event of winning. `[snippet]` — https://www.asc.ohio-state.edu/kagel.4/CVsurvey.short.PDF Salvage auctions have the defining common-value features: a value that is substantially common (parts value, export value, sc

**C16. A salvage vehicle is close to a common-value good (resale, parts and scrap value are roughly the same for every bidder, but each bidder estimates it with error), which is exactly the setting in which the winner's curse appears and persists even among professionals.** Kagel and Levin's survey reports that naive bidders initially incur large losses that decline with experience, but that the curse persists for experienced and professional participants, producing below-normal or negative average profits. The operational implication is that bidding up to one's own point estimate of value is

**E8. In second-price-style auctions, increasing the number of bidders produced no change in individual bidding, contrary to the Nash prediction that bids should fall — a direct warning against proxy-bid complacency.** Reported for second-price sealed-bid auctions (Kagel, Levin and Harstad, 1995). https://www.asc.ohio-state.edu/kagel.4/CVsurvey.short.PDF

**B5. The buyer-fee load is material to the arithmetic, not a rounding error.** Copart's FY1996 10-K stated that approximately 27% of revenues that year were attributable to buyer fees. (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000900075/000091205796023870/0000912057-96-023870.txt) Current published fee schedules are not machine-readable from copart.com; third-party calculators put the 2026 load at a tiered buyer fee, a gate fee of roughly $79 (clean title) to $95 (non-clean title), a tiered virtual bid fee, and a ~$15 environmental fee. (https://vininfohub.com/copart-fees-explained; https://w

**A2. Storage cost begins accruing on a schedule measured in business days, not weeks, and escalates.** Copart's buyer terms set storage at $5/day starting after 3 business days for online purchases (2 business days for kiosk/Buy It Now), rising to $30/day and upward after 10 days. `[read]` — https://www.copart.com/content/us/en/pdfs/terms&conditions-2019.pdf IAA's Canadian arm applies a per-vehicle, per-day storage fee "starting from the day after the sale day if the Vehicle is not removed within 3 business days." `[read]` — https://ca.iaai.com/Content/Documents/IAAPoliciesJuly2020_en.pdf *Fa

**C4. Bids are irrevocable and a bidder can be made to pay for bidding against themselves.** Copart: "Once a bid has been submitted, it cannot be retracted, deleted, or cancelled.
